test_title: PYST 6: SSC CHSL - General Awareness (Held On: 13 April 2021 Shift 3)
subject: gk
question: Which of the following statements regarding the functioning of Rajya Sabha is correct?

options.text: Rajya Sabha is not subject to dissolution.
Rajya Sabha is dissolved after the assent of the President of India.
Rajya Sabha is dissolved every second year.
Rajya Sabha is dissolved after the dissolution of the Lok Sabha.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajya Sabha is not subject to dissolution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Rajya Sabha is not subject to dissolution, with one-third of its members retiring every other year**__.

 __
 
• The Rajya Sabha should have no more than 250 members - 238 members represent states and union territories, and 12 members are nominated by the President.
 
• The members of the Rajya Sabha are elected by the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the States and Union Territories in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote.
 
• The Rajya Sabha can also initiate legislation and a bill is required to be passed by the Rajya Sabha to become a law.
 
• The Rajya Sabha is the representative of the states in the union legislature.
 
• The Rajya Sabha has powers that protect the rights of the states against the union.
 
• Smt. Rukmini Devi Arundale was the first woman nominated member of the Rajya Sabha.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ​The Lok Sabha has certain powers that make it more powerful than the Rajya Sabha.
 
 
• Motions of no confidence against the government can be introduced and passed in the Lok Sabha.
 
• If passed by a majority vote, the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers resign collectively.
 
 
 
• **Parliamentary Committees of the Rajya Sabha may be categorized as ad hoc Committees and Standing Committees.**
 
 
• Ad hoc Committees are those Committees that may be constituted by the House or by the Chairman or by the Presiding Officers of both Houses jointly to consider and report on specific matters.
 
 
• Such Committees become functus officio as soon as they complete their work. 
 
 
 
• **Standing Committees **are permanent committees whose members are either elected by the House or nominated by the Chairman every year or from time to time.
 
 
• These are: Business Advisory Committee, General Purposes Committee, Committee on Government assurances, House Committee, Committee on Petitions, Committee on Subordinate Legislation, Committee on Papers Laid on the Table, Committee of Privileges, Committee on Rules, Committee on Ethics, Committee on Provision of Computers to Members of Rajya Sabha, Committee on Member of Parliament for Local Area Development Scheme and the Department-related Standing Committees
 
 
 
 

8d
